A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSCAR and have readable main text, equations and figures. However, v4 ends with references on page 12 and v5 on page 13; neither includes the repeatedly referenced appendices containing derivations, algorithms and supplementary comparisons.

before.justification: V4 reports original OSCAR compression results on Kodak, DIV2K-val and CLIC2020, together with efficiency comparisons and component ablations.

after.justification: V5 reports original compression and ablation results, plus bitrate-adaptation experiments and PSNR/FID comparisons.

M1.justification: The core architecture, losses and two-stage procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds a limited extension procedure for unseen bitrates: continued fine-tuning samples the new bitrate with probability 0.5 and existing rates with probability 0.5.

E1.justification: Training datasets and the three evaluation datasets remain unchanged. V5 adds a sequential adaptation scenario at previously unseen bitrates, testing whether new rates can be learned while retaining performance at existing rates, rather than only evaluating the predefined rate set.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds evaluated IPIC and DDCM comparisons and an uncompressed VAE reconstruction reference for PSNR. Figure 5 retains its comparator membership. PerCo (SD) is newly identified as the implementation used for the existing PerCo baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported second-stage batch size from 32 to 64 and training iterations from 100,000 to 150,000. V5 also expands the evaluated rate grid, adds PSNR and CLIC2020-only FID evaluation, and specifies 15,000-iteration adaptation with balanced new/existing-rate sampling. These substantially revise the documented experimental settings without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8b adds sequential adaptation to 0.051 and 0.109 bpp, examining new-rate learning and degradation at previously trained rates. Figure 9 adds a VAE reconstruction control relevant to PSNR limitations. The original mapping, representation-alignment and loss ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The existing residual-distribution and cosine-similarity displays are retained, with no new run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The explanation for restricting FID to CLIC2020 concerns evaluation design and does not provide an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Figure 5 revises OSCAR's rate-quality curves and expands its Kodak operating points from four to eight. Figures 8b and 9 newly report adaptation outcomes and PSNR/FID results. Figure 6 changes the second OSCAR example's bitrate label from 0.051 to 0.043 bpp while retaining the image. The changed training settings prevent interpreting revised scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The displayed equations (1)-(16), quantization-noise assumptions and cosine-similarity reasoning are unchanged. Both versions refer to a full appendix derivation that is absent from the supplied PDFs, preventing a reliable comparison of the referenced proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: one-step diffusion decoding, a shared generative backbone across bitrates, and favorable reconstruction quality and efficiency. The stated novelty and main contributions are not redefined.

C2.justification: V5 explains non-convex rate-distortion curves through the interaction of downsampling ratio and codebook size. It also attributes PSNR limitations to VAE reconstruction, qualifies unseen-rate support through additional training, and explains why small evaluation datasets are unsuitable for stable FID estimation.

D1.justification: V5 changes the code/model statement from a promised release to reported availability, identifies the PerCo (SD) implementation, and updates second-stage hardware from four to eight RTX A6000 GPUs. Conversely, it omits v4's description of the discriminator's pretrained U-Net encoder and lightweight MLP head.

R1.justification: V5 adds references for Cold Diffusion, PerCo (SD), DDCM, IPIC and Sohl-Dickstein et al.'s diffusion work, while removing the iterative-super-resolution and conditional-control references. The related-work narrative and core novelty positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: V5 condenses the dataset and metric descriptions into one paragraph, shortens representation-alignment explanations, updates affiliations and the conference designation, and adds acknowledgments. The main section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with revised axes and legend ordering. Figure 8 combines the retained alignment plots with new adaptation panels, and Figure 9 is added. Figure 1's caption is shortened, with limited page reflow; the existing qualitative images and core diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The adaptation experiments and PSNR/FID comparisons provide better support for bitrate flexibility and a more balanced account of reconstruction limitations. These gains outweigh the limited loss of discriminator implementation detail. The referenced appendices remain unavailable, and the revised training budget limits direct interpretation of performance changes.
